source.title: Spectral Dynamics in Deep Networks: Feature Learning, Outlier Escape, and Learning Rate Transfer
source.authors: Clarissa Lauditi; Cengiz Pehlevan; Blake Bordelon

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and experimental details.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a portion of V5 by measuring learning-rate transfer and top-NTK-mode dynamics across widths and parameterizations; it does not test the stated above-stability loss trajectory.
record.gate_note: The paper reports spectral dynamics and learning-rate-transfer results. Its CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and language-model results concern weight spectra and loss dynamics, not training classification error; they do not qualify as rows for V1–V4 or V6.
record.test_reason: The study uses the edge-of-stability connection between learning rate and the leading NTK eigenvalue to explain learning-rate transfer. Its results measure width-dependent stability limits and spectral sharpening, without establishing any of V5's specified loss-and-curvature trajectories. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the learning-rate-transfer results: µP produces more width-consistent outlier and leading-NTK dynamics than NTK-P in proportionally wide linear networks. The broader paper develops a spectral theory for dependent spikes and shows that extensive-output tasks can restructure the spectral bulk.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies spectral dynamics and width-dependent learning-rate transfer, rather than the above-stability loss behavior in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Parameterization (µP versus NTK-P), width ratio ν, and learning rate η affect the reported spectral and transfer dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: The maximum stable learning rate varies weakly across width ratios in µP and strongly in NTK-P, with predictions based on the leading NTK mode.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameterization controls width consistency of stable learning rates in proportionally wide linear networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-BBP leading NTK dynamics are nearly width-independent in µP and width-dependent in NTK-P; larger learning rates accelerate sharpening toward edge of stability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameterization and learning rate govern spectral sharpening and its consistency across widths.

record.problems: The relevant results are reported qualitatively in figure descriptions without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The study does not measure the above-stability loss trajectories described by V5.
record.rows_left_out: No other results meet the row criteria for the claim versions: CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and language-model results concern spectra or loss dynamics rather than the training-error, initialization-speed, depth-error, or normalization outcomes named by the versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including random labels and dependence on size, stopping time, or regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, prevention through identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization preventing vanishing or exploding signals, training-speed and depth comparisons, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.

Above-initial-stability loss rise followed by curvature reduction and recovery; divergence at larger rates; sharpness hovering at the stability threshold while loss continues falling; and divergence despite starting below the threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free alternative.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V5 labels. Width-dependent transfer is neither support for nor a limitation of V5, and sharpening toward a threshold alone does not establish the loss dynamics that version specifies.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including corrupted or random labels and comparisons by model size, stopping time, or regularization.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU spurious minima and extra student width.
Plain versus residual networks' training error across depth; special initializations and normalization-free training as described.
Activation-matched initialization, training speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Does not report the above-stability squared-loss rise-and-recovery trajectory, sharpness hovering at the stability threshold during continued loss decline, or runs diverging below the threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy and learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup training without normalization.

rows.operation_detail: Tracked the top NTK eigenvalue over training time and learning rates.

rows.value: In µP, post-BBP dynamics are nearly ν-independent; in NTK-P they remain strongly ν-dependent and approach a lazy large-ν limit. Larger η speeds up sharpening until edge-of-stability.
rows.note: The text reports qualitative behavior, without numerical values for the plotted trajectories.
rows.check: Figure 5 reports progressive NTK sharpening toward edge of stability, but does not establish hovering at the threshold while training loss continues falling. Its caption identifies panel (c) as a weight-covariance eigenvalue plot, so the row should not describe every panel as measuring the top NTK eigenvalue.

relation.reason: The introduction uses the relationship between stability and the leading NTK eigenvalue as a premise for studying hyperparameter transfer.

tranche.reason: The study uses the edge-of-stability connection to explain width-dependent learning-rate transfer. Its spectral results do not establish V5's loss recovery or sustained threshold-hovering trajectories, and do not test another listed version.

source_check.notes: Figure 4(a) specifically concerns SGD. The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate; qualitative spectral sharpening alone does not establish V5's joint loss-and-curvature behavior.
